title: Dr. Jyoti Bajpai: Redefining Cancer Care Through Precision, Purpose and Compassion

contentHtml:
Oncologist of the Year | ET Healthcare Awards 2026“Science gives us the tools to fight cancer; humanity gives us the purpose.”Cancer treatment is advancing rapidly, from genomic profiling and targeted therapies to immunotherapy and precision medicine. Yet for Dr. Jyoti Bajpai, progress in oncology cannot be measured by scientific breakthroughs alone. Its true value lies in whether those advances help patients live longer, live better and navigate uncertainty with greater confidence.

Recognised as Oncologist of the Year at the ET Healthcare Awards 2026, Dr. Bajpai views the honour as a reflection of a collective effort involving patients, families and clinical teams. Her professional journey, beginning at AIIMS and spanning nearly two decades at Tata Memorial Centre before moving to Apollo Hospitals, has been shaped by extensive clinical experience and international exposure. Her training and engagements at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC), New York, in immuno-oncology and melanoma; Johns Hopkins, Maryland, in sarcomas; the University of Chicago; and ESMO in gynaecological malignancies and precision therapies have further enriched her expertise. Through these experiences, she has remained committed to a guiding principle: scientific excellence must always be rooted in humanity.

Advt

Her work spans precision oncology, immunotherapy, clinical research, breast and gynaecological cancers, sarcomas, gastrointestinal malignancies, and complex and rare cancers. Through clinical practice and international collaborations, she seeks to contribute not only to individual patient outcomes but also to the evolution of cancer treatment standards.

Precision begins with the right treatment, not the newest one

One of oncology's most significant shifts has been the move from treating cancers primarily according to their site of origin to understanding the biological mechanisms driving them. Patients with the same cancer may have different molecular alterations, immune profiles and responses to treatment. Genomic profiling, targeted therapies and immunotherapy have expanded options for appropriately selected patients.

For Dr. Bajpai, however, precision oncology is not about ordering every available test or prescribing the latest medicine. It is about identifying which investigations can genuinely inform a decision, interpreting findings against the available evidence and weighing potential benefits against individual needs and circumstances.The distinction is particularly important when treatments are expensive or evidence remains limited. A promising molecular finding does not automatically translate into an effective therapy, and the newest or costliest intervention is not necessarily the most appropriate. The objective is to identify the treatment most likely to benefit the individual patient.

Advt

This principle becomes even more critical in rare and complex cancers, where established protocols may not provide clear answers. Accurate diagnosis, expert pathology review, appropriate molecular characterisation and multidisciplinary discussions help establish a sound basis for treatment. Clinical trials and international expertise may provide further options where relevant.Patients and families, meanwhile, need honest conversations about risks, benefits, alternatives and uncertainty. Hope must remain part of cancer care, but it must be grounded in evidence rather than false promises.

Turning scientific breakthroughs into meaningful outcomes

Precision medicines, immunotherapy and antibody-drug conjugates are reshaping treatment possibilities for selected cancers. Their impact depends on identifying the right patients, establishing stronger evidence for treatment combinations and sequencing, improving biomarkers and ensuring clinical trials represent diverse patient populations.

Advt

Access to quality molecular testing and innovative therapies remains equally important. A breakthrough has limited value if patients who could benefit from it cannot obtain it.Dr. Bajpai's engagement with the Advanced Breast Cancer (ABC) international consensus initiative, the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer (SITC) connects her clinical work with evolving international evidence and standards. As Founder and President-elect of the Immuno-Oncology Society of India (I-OSI), she is also committed to strengthening India's capabilities in immuno-oncology.

Her focus reflects a wider ambition: to help translate emerging knowledge into clinical practice while contributing Indian expertise to international discussions on cancer treatment. Scientific innovation, in her view, becomes meaningful when it produces better outcomes for patients, rather than remaining confined to laboratories or research publications.

Beyond the tumour: The person behind the diagnosis

Cancer affects far more than physical health. It can reshape fertility choices, relationships, careers, finances, body image and a person's sense of the future. A young adult may be concerned about parenthood, while a woman undergoing breast cancer treatment may worry about body image or returning to work. For an older patient, preserving independence and everyday function may be as important as tumour response.These concerns require attention alongside medical treatment. Psychological support, fertility counselling, symptom management and survivorship planning should be considered early, not treated as secondary additions to care.For Dr. Bajpai, quality of life is central to the purpose of oncology. Extending survival remains essential, but the experience of those additional years matters too. Treatment decisions must account for the life patients hope to return to, their preferences and the trade-offs they are willing to accept.Compassion, therefore, is not separate from clinical excellence. It is an essential part of applying medical knowledge responsibly to each patient's circumstances.

India's opportunity to shape the future of oncology

India's clinical expertise, expanding diagnostic capabilities and diverse patient population offer significant opportunities to contribute to globally relevant cancer research. Dr. Bajpai sees further potential in the convergence of precision medicine, immunotherapy, AI-enabled clinical decision support and stronger research capabilities.However, technology alone cannot guarantee progress. Affordability, access, research quality and appropriate clinical use must advance alongside innovation. AI and data-driven tools may support clinical decisions, but their value depends on reliable evidence and sound medical judgement.Through international collaborations and her work with I-OSI, Dr. Bajpai aims to strengthen national expertise, encourage research and build capabilities in immuno-oncology. The ambition is not merely to adopt advances developed elsewhere, but to contribute Indian clinical experience to global knowledge while ensuring that progress reaches a broader patient population.

Recognition as a continuing responsibility

Dr. Bajpai's patients have taught her that courage is not the absence of fear, but the ability to move forward despite uncertainty. They have also reinforced the importance of humility in a field where even remarkable scientific advances cannot guarantee identical outcomes for everyone.Research, mentoring, collaboration and compassionate practice must work together. A treatment plan is incomplete unless patients understand it, trust its rationale and can realistically access the care it requires.The Oncologist of the Year recognition acknowledges her contribution to clinical practice, research and patient-centred cancer care. For Dr. Bajpai, its significance lies in the responsibility it reinforces: to pursue better treatments without confusing novelty with benefit, to offer hope without overstating what medicine can promise, and to never allow the complexity of a disease to overshadow the person experiencing it.Science will continue to expand the possibilities of cancer care.
